newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga weighs further Snorre development.
newsitem.headline: Saga weighs further Snorre development.

text.p: Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it may develop Snorre's four northernmost fault blocks and that the North Sea oilfield could extend further south than previously thought.

"Recoverable oil reserves in the four fault blocks are put at roughly 250 million barrels, which will yield roughly 100,000 barrels per day," Paal Hansen-Tangen, manager of the Snorre II project, told Saga Information newsletter.
"Reserve estimates will be affected by the development solution and drive mechanism selected," he said.

A delineation well is planned on Snorre's northern flank in early 1997 to reduce uncertainty over reserves in this area. At the same time a Vigdis well will be extended northwards in a bid to delineate the southern extent of Snorre, Saga said.

"A decision on further development will be taken in the context of a long-term offtake solution for the whole Snorre field," Hansen-Tangen said. "Final processing of Snorre output is currently due to be transferred from Statfjord A to the B platform in 2003."

A preliminary assessment of solutions was made as part of the Snorre long-term plan in the first half of this year. The licensees voted in June to look more closely at four options, all based on subsea production.
The plan calls for a subsea development of the northern flank -- and possibly the southern area -- with a switch from Statoil's Statfjord A to B in 2003.

Saga said one alternative was to install a spur or a separate flowline from Snorre to Statfjord B in 1999 to permit parallel processing and thereby expand production capacity from the Snorre field. The possibility of tying a subsea development directly to Statfjord B will also be assessed, it said.
Last month Saga said it had upgraded recoverable reserve estimates at Snorre by 16 percent to 1.315 billion barrels.
The new figure was 71 percent higher than the original estimate of 767 million barrels, which formed the basis for the decision to develop the field in 1988.
The company attributed the upgrade to new technology, improved geological understanding of the reservoir and new, advanced production methods.
Saga, as operator of Snorre, holds an 11.94 percent stake in the field.

Other partners are Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) with 41.40 percent, Esso Norge AS XON.NX with 10.33 percent, Deminex Norge AS with 10.03 percent, Idemitsu Petroleum Norge AS with 9.60 percent, Norsk Hydro NHY.OL Produksjon ASA with 8.27 percent, Elf Petroleum Norge AS with 5.51 percent, Amerada Hess Corp Norge AS with 1.46 percent and Enterprise Oil Plc Norwegian AS with 1.46 percent.
